title: AI & Learning English in 2026 (English Listening Practice)
speaker: Alastair Budge

sentences.en: Hello, hello, hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English, the show where you can listen to fascinating stories and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 你好，你好，你好，欢迎收听由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》，在这个节目里，你可以聆听精彩的故事，了解世界上奇妙而有趣的事物，同时还能提升你的英语水平。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about AI and learning English.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊一聊人工智能与英语学习。

sentences.en: Now, we’ve talked about this before, back in 2022, but that seems like centuries ago in the era of AI.
sentences.zh: 其实我们在 2022 年就讨论过这个话题，但在人工智能时代，那感觉好像已经是几个世纪前的事了。

sentences.en: So in today’s episode we are going to talk about what has changed, what hasn’t changed, and how AI can and can’t help you improve your English in 2026.
sentences.zh: 所以在今天的节目中，我们将讨论哪些变了，哪些没变，以及在 2026 年人工智能如何能（以及不能）帮助你提高英语水平。

sentences.en: OK then, let's not waste a minute and get right into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，那我们一分钟也不浪费，直接切入正题吧。

sentences.en: I want you to cast your mind back to late 2022.
sentences.zh: 我想让你把思绪拉回到 2022 年底。

sentences.en: The world was watching anxiously as the Russian invasion of Ukraine looked to be ratcheting up a notch.
sentences.zh: 当时世界正焦虑地看着俄罗斯对乌克兰的入侵似乎进一步升级。

sentences.en: Inflation looked like it might be spiralling out of control.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀看起来可能要失控。

sentences.en: In the UK, a tabloid newspaper set up a livestream of an iceberg lettuce and a picture of the then Prime Minister, Liz Truss, asking its viewers which would last longer, the lettuce or the PM.
sentences.zh: 在英国，一家小报开启了一场直播，画面中有一个生菜头和时任首相 Liz Truss 的照片，询问观众究竟哪个能撑得更久，是生菜还是首相。

sentences.en: By the way, the lettuce won. And then in late November, quietly at first, a company called OpenAI launched a chatbot called ChatGPT.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，生菜赢了。然后在那年 11 月底，一家名为 OpenAI 的公司悄悄推出了一款名为 ChatGPT 的聊天机器人。

sentences.en: Within five days, a million people had used it.
sentences.zh: 短短五天内，就有一百万人使用过它。

sentences.en: I was one of them, and perhaps you were too.
sentences.zh: 我是其中之一，也许你也是。

sentences.en: It seemed like magic. You could type in a question, any question, and you would get an answer back.
sentences.zh: 这看起来就像魔法。你可以输入一个问题，任何问题，然后就能得到回答。

sentences.en: Help me write this email. What’s the capital of Uzbekistan?
sentences.zh: 帮我写封邮件。乌兹别克斯坦的首都是哪里？

sentences.en: Why is grass green? Now, the answers weren't always right.
sentences.zh: 为什么草是绿色的？当然，答案并不总是对的。

sentences.en: Sometimes they were plain wrong. But it was a window into the future, a future in which knowledge, intelligence, was available to anyone, anywhere, in a way that it never had been before.
sentences.zh: 有时它们完全是错的。但这却是通往未来的一扇窗，在那个未来里，知识和智能可以被任何人、在任何地方获取，这是以前从未有过的。

sentences.en: And it didn’t take long for people to start thinking about how this new technology could be applied to the world of language learning.
sentences.zh: 人们没花多久就开始思考这项新技术如何才能应用到语言学习的世界中。

sentences.en: Indeed, just a couple of weeks after the release of ChatGPT we made an episode on exactly this, imaginatively called “Artificial Intelligence & Language Learning”.
sentences.zh: 事实上，就在 ChatGPT 发布几周后，我们就制作了一期专门谈论这个的节目，名字很富有想象力，叫作《人工智能与语言学习》。

sentences.en: That was three and a half years ago, and things have moved on a lot since then.
sentences.zh: 那是三年半前的事了，从那以后，事情已经有了很大的进展。

sentences.en: The technology has improved significantly, there are many things that are possible now that weren’t even a few months ago.
sentences.zh: 技术有了显著的提升，现在许多事情是甚至在几个月前都无法实现的。

sentences.en: But with these improvements come pitfalls, traps I have seen plenty of people fall into, so we will talk about those too.
sentences.zh: 但伴随着这些进步而来的也是陷阱，我看到很多人掉进这些陷阱里，所以我们也会谈谈这些。

sentences.en: Now, a quick administrative note before we get too far into it.
sentences.zh: 好了，在深入探讨之前，先做一个简单的说明。

sentences.en: I’m not going to talk too much about specific AI tools, ChatGPT vs.
sentences.zh: 我不会过多讨论具体的人工智能工具，比如 ChatGPT 对比

sentences.en: Gemini or Claude, or any of the speaking apps, because they all do pretty similar things, and the best one right now might not be the best one by the time you listen to this, so what I’m about to say should apply to whatever AI tool you are using.
sentences.zh: Gemini 或是 Claude，或者任何口语应用，因为它们的功能都差不多，而且现在最好的工具等你听到这期节目时可能已经不是最好的了，所以我接下来要说的话适用于你正在使用的任何人工智能工具。

sentences.en: I’m also going to be talking relatively generally, rather than going into specific prompts and exercises.
sentences.zh: 我也将进行比较概括的探讨，而不是深入探讨具体的提示词和练习。

sentences.en: If you’d like specific tips and tricks, then there are a bunch of tutorials over on our YouTube channel - I’ll put a link to that in the description for this episode.
sentences.zh: 如果你想要具体的技巧和诀窍，那么我们的 YouTube 频道上有许多教程——我会在本期节目的简介中放一个链接。

sentences.en: OK, with those disclaimers out of the way, let’s start by going through it semi-systematically.
sentences.zh: 好了，抛开这些免责声明，让我们开始半系统性地梳理一下。

sentences.en: The way that many people think about language competency is through the four pillars of reading, writing, listening and speaking.
sentences.zh: 许多人思考语言能力的方式是通过阅读、写作、听力和口语这四大支柱。

sentences.en: This is a helpful framing, but I think it’s even more helpful to split it into just two: input and output, with reading and listening in the input category, and writing and speaking in the output category.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很有帮助的框架，但我认为把它简化为输入和输出两个类别会更有用：阅读和听力属于输入类别，写作和口语属于输出类别。

sentences.en: I think this is a useful framework for thinking about where AI can fit in, especially as almost everyone finds output harder than input; it’s easier to understand English than it is to produce it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个有用的框架，可以用来思考人工智能可以切入的位置，尤其是几乎每个人都觉得输出比输入更难；理解英语比产出英语要容易得多。

sentences.en: So, let’s start with input: reading first, and then listening.
sentences.zh: 所以，让我们从输入开始：先是阅读，然后是听力。

sentences.en: Back in 2022, AI was already quite good at dealing with text.
sentences.zh: 早在 2022 年，人工智能就已经很擅长处理文本了。

sentences.en: You could paste in an article and ask for a summary.
sentences.zh: 你可以粘贴一篇文章并要求生成摘要。

sentences.en: You could ask it to explain a difficult word.
sentences.zh: 你可以要求它解释一个难词。

sentences.en: You could even ask it to simplify something into B1-level English.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以要求它把内容简化为 B1 级别的英语。

sentences.en: Super helpful, and that hasn’t changed. What has changed is the scale, the speed, and the integration.
sentences.zh: 超级有用，而且这一点没有改变。改变的是规模、速度和集成度。

sentences.en: In 2026, almost every website, every app, every browser, has some form of AI built in.
sentences.zh: 在 2026 年，几乎每个网站、每个应用、每个浏览器都内置了某种形式的人工智能。

sentences.en: You can highlight a paragraph and get an explanation instantly.
sentences.zh: 你可以高亮一段文字并立即得到解释。

sentences.en: You can generate a vocabulary list in seconds.
sentences.zh: 你可以在几秒钟内生成词汇表。

sentences.en: You can ask follow-up questions and have a conversation about what you’ve just read.
sentences.zh: 你可以提出后续问题，并就你刚读过的内容进行对话。

sentences.en: From a purely technical perspective, this is extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 从纯技术的角度来看，这是非同寻常的。

sentences.en: But here is the first important point: AI makes it very easy to consume content without it actually sticking, without you actually learning from it.
sentences.zh: 但这里是第一个重要的点：人工智能让人类非常容易消费内容，却没有真正将其内化，没有真正从中学习。

sentences.en: You might understand something in the moment, perhaps you feel like you've learned it, but then, surprise surprise, you forget it.
sentences.zh: 你当时可能理解了，也许你觉得自己学会了，但随后，意料之外情理之中，你把它忘了。

sentences.en: It's gone. So if you're using AI to help you read and understand English, make sure you're doing something with what you are taught.
sentences.zh: 它消失了。所以，如果你正在使用人工智能来帮助你阅读和理解英语，请确保你对所学的内容做点什么。

sentences.en: That might be writing the phrase down, using it in a sentence, making sure you come back to it a few days later.
sentences.zh: 这可能包括把短语写下来、在句子中使用它、确保几天后再回来复习。

sentences.en: Doing everything you can to use it actively, the same as in the pre-AI era.
sentences.zh: 尽你所能去积极地使用它，这和人工智能出现之前是一样的。

sentences.en: And in fact, there’s one more thing, something you should do before you even think about using AI to explain something: force yourself to guess first, to really think about what the answer could be.
sentences.zh: 事实上，还有一件事，这是你在考虑让人工智能解释某事之前就应该做的：强迫自己先去猜测，去真正思考答案可能是什么。

sentences.en: If you come across a difficult expression, try to work out the meaning from the context before asking AI.
sentences.zh: 如果你遇到一个困难的表达，在问人工智能之前，试着从上下文中推断出它的意思。

sentences.en: If it’s a tricky grammar point, try to really THINK about what the rule is, then ask AI to check if you're right.
sentences.zh: 如果是一个棘手的语法点，试着去真正思考规则是什么，然后让人工智能检查你是否正确。

sentences.en: This transforms AI from an answer machine into a tutor.
sentences.zh: 这把人工智能从一个答题机器变成了一位导师。

sentences.en: You're thinking actively, not just consuming passively, so you are much more likely to retain the information, you’re much more likely to actually learn.
sentences.zh: 你在积极思考，而不仅仅是被动消费，所以你更有可能记住这些信息，更有可能真正学到东西。

sentences.en: It’s a similar story with listening, although there are some additional complications and opportunities.
sentences.zh: 听力的情况也类似，尽管有一些额外的复杂性和机遇。

sentences.en: The main thing to say is that text to speech technology, which is the technology that takes text and converts it to spoken language, this has improved dramatically since 2022.
sentences.zh: 最主要的是，文字转语音技术（即把文字转换为口语的技术）自 2022 年以来已经有了极大的改善。

sentences.en: Back then, AI voices sounded robotic. Obvious.
sentences.zh: 当时，人工智能的声音听起来很机械。非常明显。

sentences.en: It was quite painful to listen to. Today, synthetic speech is almost indistinguishable from a real human voice.
sentences.zh: 听起来相当痛苦。如今，合成语音几乎与真实的人类声音无法区分。

sentences.en: You can slow it down naturally. You can change accents.
sentences.zh: 你可以自然地放慢语速。你可以改变口音。

sentences.en: You can even interrupt it mid-sentence and ask it for clarification.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可以在句子中途打断它并要求它澄清。

sentences.en: This can be incredibly useful, especially for people at lower levels, let’s say anyone up to B1 or so.
sentences.zh: 这可能非常有用，尤其是对水平较低的人来说，比方说 B1 或以下的人。

sentences.en: Most of the AI tools, from ChatGPT to Gemini, they have a voice mode, where you can have a conversation about whatever you want.
sentences.zh: 大多数人工智能工具，从 ChatGPT 到 Gemini，都有语音模式，你可以在其中就任何你想要的话题进行对话。

sentences.en: We’ll talk about this more in a few minutes, when we talk about speaking, but for the purposes of listening, these models have come on leaps and bounds since 2022.
sentences.zh: 几分钟后当我们谈论口语时会更多地讨论这一点，但就听力而言，自 2022 年以来，这些模型已经取得了长足的进步。

sentences.en: The accents are better, it sounds more natural, and most importantly, it gives you 24/7 access to an endlessly patient and friendly source of English input.
sentences.zh: 口音更好了，听起来更自然，最重要的是，它为你提供了全天候的无限耐心且友好的英语输入来源。

sentences.en: But if you are listening to this show, AI-generated English might be a little frustrating.
sentences.zh: 但如果你在听这个节目，人工智能生成的英语可能会有点令人沮丧。

sentences.en: You are at a level where you can understand a lot of native-level content, and sometimes AI-generated content is painfully obvious.
sentences.zh: 你已经处于能够理解大量母语级别内容的水平，有时人工智能生成的内容简直错得或者假得显而易见。

sentences.en: If you’ve ever been confronted with these AI-generated podcasts on YouTube, you’ll know exactly what I mean.
sentences.zh: 如果你曾经在 YouTube 上遇到过这些人工智能生成的播客，你就会明白我的意思。

sentences.en: And here’s the danger. If you spend too much time listening to simplified AI-generated English, your brain will adapt to simplified English.
sentences.zh: 危险就在这里。如果你花太多时间听简化后的人工智能生成英语，你的大脑就会适应这种简化的英语。

sentences.en: Or English that sounds like someone is reading out what is meant to be a written article.
sentences.zh: 或者听起来像是有人在宣读本该是书面文章的英语。

sentences.en: AI generated audio will undoubtedly improve in the future, but at the moment it’s great for single words or single sentences, but anything longer than that is usually pretty easy to recognise.
sentences.zh: 人工智能生成的音频在未来无疑会改善，但目前它对于单个单词或单个句子很棒，但任何比这更长的内容通常都很容易被识别出来。

sentences.en: It’s not the English that you’ll find in the real world, English that’s full of ums and ahs, people changing what they want to say mid-sentence, mumbling, being interrupted, real, raw, native English.
sentences.zh: 这不是你在现实世界中会遇到的英语，现实世界中的英语充满了嗯和啊、人们在句子中途改变想说的话、嘟囔、被打断，这是真实、生动、地道的英语。

sentences.en: So here’s how I think about it. The best way to improve your listening skills remains to listen to real, human, raw English, whether that’s podcasts, YouTube, audiobooks, TV, or whatever else.
sentences.zh: 所以我是这样看待它的。提高你听力技能的最佳方法依然是聆听真实的、人类的、生动的英语，无论是播客、YouTube、有声书、电视还是其他什么。

sentences.en: But to use AI as a way to scaffold, to build on this, and support your listening.
sentences.zh: 但要将人工智能作为一种脚手架来使用，在此基础之上构建并支持你的听力。

sentences.en: Let me give you a concrete example of how this can work with podcasts, because I think this is one of the most powerful uses of AI, and clearly it’s relevant to you, because you are listening to one right now.
sentences.zh: 让我举一个具体的例子，看看这如何与播客协同工作，因为我认为这是人工智能最强大的用途之一，而且显然这与你息息相关，因为你现在就在听一个。

sentences.en: So, first, listen to the episode normally.
sentences.zh: 所以，首先，正常地听这期节目。

sentences.en: Don't look at the transcript yet. Then, before looking at the transcript, open up ChatGPT and try to summarise what you heard.
sentences.zh: 先不要看文本。然后，在看文本之前，打开 ChatGPT 并试着总结你听到的内容。

sentences.en: THEN paste in the full transcript and ask it to find 10 natural expressions that native speakers use; not just vocabulary words, but actual phrases.
sentences.zh: 然后粘贴完整的文本，让它找出母语者使用的 10 个自然表达；不仅仅是词汇，而是真正的短语。

sentences.en: For each expression, get AI to explain what it means and show you how to use it in a different context.
sentences.zh: 对于每个表达，让人工智能解释它的意思，并向你展示如何在不同的语境中使用它。

sentences.en: Then, create a fill-in-the-blank exercise where you practise using those expressions.
sentences.zh: 然后，创建一个填空练习，练习使用这些表达。

sentences.en: Finally, get AI to give you a discussion question about the episode topic, and practise answering it.
sentences.zh: 最后，让人工智能给你出一个关于节目主题的讨论问题，并练习回答它。

sentences.en: This can turn 20 or 30 minutes of passive listening into an hour plus of active learning.
sentences.zh: 这可以将 20 或 30 分钟的被动听力变成一小时以上的主动学习。

sentences.en: And you can do this with literally any podcast or video that has a transcript.
sentences.zh: 你字面意义上可以用任何有文本的播客或视频来做这件事。

sentences.en: And by the way, you can find lots of demos and tutorials of how to do this on our YouTube channel.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你可以在我们的 YouTube 频道上找到许多关于如何做到这一点的演示和教程。

sentences.en: There’s a link in the description to that.
sentences.zh: 简介里有那个的链接。

sentences.en: Now let's turn to output, writing and speaking, and let’s start with writing.
sentences.zh: 现在让我们转向输出，即写作和口语，先从写作开始。

sentences.en: Writing is where AI has perhaps made the biggest leap forward for English learners, and where I think the benefits are most clear-cut.
sentences.zh: 在写作方面，人工智能可能为英语学习者迈出了最大的一步，而且我认为其好处也最为明确。

sentences.en: But again, there are some pretty obvious pitfalls.
sentences.zh: 但同样，也有一些非常明显的陷阱。

sentences.en: So, the old way of improving your English writing was essentially to learn grammar and vocabulary, through textbooks and reading widely.
sentences.zh: 所以，过去提高英语写作的方法基本上是通过教科书和广泛阅读来学习语法和词汇。

sentences.en: And to turn that acquired knowledge, those building blocks of language, into written text.
sentences.zh: 并将习得的知识、语言的这些构建模块转化为书面文本。

sentences.en: You’d write something. But you wouldn’t be sure if it was right.
sentences.zh: 你会写点东西。但你不会确定它是否正确。

sentences.en: Maybe you weren’t sure you’d used the right tense, or whether this was how a native speaker would have written it.
sentences.zh: 也许你不确定自己是否用了正确的时态，或者母语者是否会这样写。

sentences.en: Perhaps you’d ask a friend, someone who was better at English than you, or even a native speaker if you were lucky.
sentences.zh: 也许你会问一个朋友，一个英语比你好的人，或者如果你幸运的话，问一个母语者。

sentences.en: Maybe you were doing an English course, and you could ask your teacher.
sentences.zh: 也许你正在参加一个英语课程，你可以问你的老师。

sentences.en: Or failing that, you might post it in a forum somewhere and wait, hoping for a kind soul to put you out of your misery.
sentences.zh: 或者如果不行，你可能会把它发到某个论坛上等待，希望有好心人能把你从痛苦中解救出来。

sentences.en: You might be lucky enough to get a response, but often the feedback wouldn’t be very helpful.
sentences.zh: 你可能会幸运地得到回复，但通常反馈并不是很有帮助。

sentences.en: Even a native speaker might not be able to tell you why something was wrong, it just was.
sentences.zh: 甚至母语者也可能无法告诉你为什么某处是错的，它就是错的。

sentences.en: Now, AI tools have made this significantly easier.
sentences.zh: 现在，人工智能工具使这变得容易多了。

sentences.en: You write something. You paste it into an AI tool, and the AI will give you a perfect, natural version.
sentences.zh: 你写了一些东西。你把它粘贴到人工智能工具中，人工智能就会给你一个完美、自然的版本。

sentences.en: Amazing, right? But the problem with this is that I see so many non-native English speakers starting to rely on AI tools to do the writing for them.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了，对吧？但问题在于，我看到太多非母语英语使用者开始依赖人工智能工具来替他们写作。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, I get tonnes of emails, mostly from non-native speakers.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的，我收到了大量的电子邮件，大多数来自非母语者。

sentences.en: It is immediately obvious to me who has used an AI to write the email for them and who hasn’t.
sentences.zh: 我一眼就能看出是谁用人工智能替他们写了邮件，谁没有。

sentences.en: And I have to admit that I am infinitely more impressed with those people who haven’t, the people who have forced themselves to produce English, even when there is the tempting option of getting an AI tool to write it for you.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认，我对那些没有使用人工智能的人、那些强迫自己产出英语的人（即使有让人工智能替你写的诱人选项）抱有无限的敬意。

sentences.en: Now, you might argue that people will just have to get used to this, and in a world where AI agents outnumber human employees, and AI-generated English continues to improve, nobody will need to actually write; an AI will do it for them.
sentences.zh: 现在，你可能会争辩说，人们以后只需要习惯这一点就行了，在一个人工智能代理数量超过人类员工、人工智能生成的英语不断改进的世界里，没有人真正需要写作；人工智能会替他们完成。

sentences.en: Even if that will some day be true, there is still an important reason to work on your writing, as a non-native speaker.
sentences.zh: 即使有朝一日这会成为现实，作为非母语者，还有一个重要的原因需要你去提升写作能力。

sentences.en: And that’s that improving your writing skills is a brilliant way of not just improving your all-round productive skills but helping you collect and distill your thoughts.
sentences.zh: 那就是，提高写作能力不仅是提升你全方位输出技能的绝佳方法，还能帮助你收集和提炼你的思想。

sentences.en: Unlike speaking, writing is an activity you can do without anyone seeing your mistakes, it’s an activity that helps build your productive muscles, and all in a safe space, because if you change what you want to say or you realise you’ve made a mistake, you can just go back and write it again.
sentences.zh: 与说话不同，写作是一项你可以不让任何人看到你犯错就能进行的活动，它是一项有助于构建你输出肌肉的活动，而且全在一个安全的环境中，因为如果你改变了你想说的话或者意识到自己犯了个错，你只需退回去重新写过。

sentences.en: And there are some great ways in which you can use AI to help you improve your writing.
sentences.zh: 有一些很棒的方法可以利用人工智能来帮助你提高写作水平。

sentences.en: Note, help you improve, not write for you.
sentences.zh: 注意，是帮你提高，而不是替你写。

sentences.en: If you use a tool like ChatGPT, you can share your writing and ask not just for a perfect version, but for explanations of the mistakes.
sentences.zh: 如果你使用像 ChatGPT 这样的工具，你可以分享你的写作，并要求它不仅提供完美的版本，还要对错误进行解释。

sentences.en: You might already use the tool that we’ve been building, FixMyEnglish.ai, which does a similar thing, but recreates the experience you might have had with a brilliant teacher, where they cross out all of your mistakes in red pen and write extensive explanations, so that you learn from every mistake.
sentences.zh: 你可能已经在使用了我们一直在构建的工具 FixMyEnglish.ai，它做的事情类似，但重现了你与一位优秀老师交流的体验，老师会用红笔划掉你所有的错误并写下详细的解释，这样你就能从每一个错误中吸取教训。

sentences.en: By the way, if you haven’t checked that out yet, you can go to FixMyEnglish.ai.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，如果你还没查看那个网站，你可以访问 FixMyEnglish.ai。

sentences.en: I’ll put a link in the show description too.
sentences.zh: 我也会在节目简介里放一个链接。

sentences.en: If you’d prefer to use ChatGPT or Gemini, or whatever AI tool you prefer, here’s how to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果你更喜欢使用 ChatGPT 或 Gemini，或者你喜欢的人工智能工具，操作方法如下。

sentences.en: First, write it yourself - mistakes and all.
sentences.zh: 首先，自己写——不管有多少错误都写下来。

sentences.en: Then, instead of asking AI to rewrite it perfectly, ask it to tell you HOW MANY mistakes you made and what TYPES of errors they are, but don't ask it to fix them just yet.
sentences.zh: 然后，与其让人工智能完美重写，不如让它告诉你你犯了多少个错误以及它们是什么类型的错误，但先不要让它修改。

sentences.en: Then, try to find and correct the mistakes based on those hints.
sentences.zh: 接着，尝试根据这些提示去寻找并纠正错误。

sentences.en: THEN get AI to show you the perfect version and explain what you missed.
sentences.zh: 然后再让人工智能向你展示完美的版本并解释你漏掉了什么。

sentences.en: This way, you are doing the learning, not the AI.
sentences.zh: 通过这种方式，是你在学习，而不是人工智能。

sentences.en: You are building the skill, not outsourcing it.
sentences.zh: 你在构建技能，而不是外包技能。

sentences.en: It takes a bit longer, of course, but that's the point - the struggle is where the learning happens.
sentences.zh: 这当然需要稍微长一点的时间，但这就是重点——挣扎的过程正是学习发生的地方。

sentences.en: Now, final point, let’s move on to talk about speaking.
sentences.zh: 现在，最后一点，让我们继续讨论口语。

sentences.en: We touched on this a little bit in the listening section, but let's go a bit deeper, because speaking is almost always the skill most people want to improve and most struggle with.
sentences.zh: 我们在听力部分稍微触及过这一点，但让我们更深入一点，因为口语几乎总是大多数人想要提高且最挣扎的技能。

sentences.en: It’s also the scariest. Speaking to a real human, a native English speaker, can be really daunting, and practising with an AI can be a very helpful stepping stone, not because AI conversation is perfect, but because the judgment is removed.
sentences.zh: 这也是最令人害怕的。与真实的人类、母语为英语的人交谈可能会让人望而生畏，而与人工智能练习可以成为一个非常有用的跳板，不是因为人工智能的对话是完美的，而是因为评判消失了。

sentences.en: So it’s hardly surprising that this, that speaking, this is the skill that so many companies are focusing on.
sentences.zh: 因此，毫不奇怪，这是口语，这是许多公司都在关注的技能。

sentences.en: And if you are anything like me, you are probably bombarded with adverts for AI-tutors with all sorts of promises, from boasts about how many billions of downloads they have to promises to make you fluent in 90 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你和我一样，你可能也会被各种人工智能导师的广告狂轰滥炸，它们有着各种各样的承诺，从吹嘘自己有多少亿下载量到承诺在 90 天内让你流利。

sentences.en: Perhaps you’ve tried a few of them yourself.
sentences.zh: 也许你已经尝试过其中一些了。

sentences.en: The dream that these apps are selling is this: you'll be able to have a real spoken conversation with an AI, it will understand your accent, respond naturally, correct your mistakes gently, and you'll emerge more fluent.
sentences.zh: 这些应用兜售的梦想是：你将能够与人工智能进行真正的口语对话，它会听懂你的口音、自然地回应、温和地纠正你的错误，然后你会变得更加流利。

sentences.en: And to be fair, the dream is closer to reality than it was in 2022.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，这个梦想比 2022 年时更接近现实了。

sentences.en: All of these tools have improved significantly.
sentences.zh: 所有这些工具都有了显著的改善。

sentences.en: The voices sound more natural. The speech recognition is much better.
sentences.zh: 声音听起来更自然了。语音识别好多了。

sentences.en: But here is what they won't tell you in the marketing materials, and what you’ve probably found out yourself if you’ve used them.
sentences.zh: 但这是他们在营销材料中不会告诉你、而如果你使用过它们的话可能自己也已经发现的事情。

sentences.en: AI conversation practice and real conversation practice are still very far from the same thing.
sentences.zh: 人工智能对话练习和真实对话练习仍然有很大差距。

sentences.en: When you talk to an AI, it is infinitely patient.
sentences.zh: 当你与人工智能交谈时，它是无限耐心的。

sentences.en: It never misunderstands you in the way a real person does.
sentences.zh: 它绝不会像真实人物那样误解你。

sentences.en: It doesn't have an agenda, it's not distracted, it doesn't use slang you've never heard, it doesn't speak faster when it gets excited.
sentences.zh: 它没有别的企图，不会分心，不会使用你从未听过的俚语，也不会在兴奋时说得更快。

sentences.en: It will wait, calmly, for as long as you need.
sentences.zh: 它会平静地等待，只要你需要多久，它就等多久。

sentences.en: That sounds like a good thing. And in many ways it is.
sentences.zh: 这听起来是件好事。在许多方面确实如此。

sentences.en: But it also means that you're practising a version of conversation that doesn't quite exist in the real world.
sentences.zh: 但这也意味着你练习的是一种在现实世界中并不完全存在的对话版本。

sentences.en: Now, none of this means these tools are useless.
sentences.zh: 现在，这并不意味着这些工具毫无用处。

sentences.en: Far from it. If you genuinely use a speaking tool every day, you will get more comfortable speaking English.
sentences.zh: 远非如此。如果你真的每天都使用口语工具，你会对说英语感到更加自在。

sentences.en: That has real value, especially if you don't have many opportunities to practise with real people.
sentences.zh: 这具有真正的价值，特别是如果你没有太多机会与真人练习的话。

sentences.en: But go in with realistic expectations, and don't let it replace real conversation.
sentences.zh: 但要抱着现实的期望去使用，不要让它取代真实的对话。

sentences.en: The way I suggest thinking about it is like a rehearsal space.
sentences.zh: 我建议的思考方式是把它当作一个排练空间。

sentences.en: Actors don't rehearse in front of an audience.
sentences.zh: 演员不会在观众面前排练。

sentences.en: They rehearse in an empty room, repeatedly, until the words feel natural.
sentences.zh: 他们在空房间里反复排练，直到台词感觉自然。

sentences.en: Then they go on stage. AI conversation can be your empty room — the place where you practise until it stops feeling frightening.
sentences.zh: 然后他们才上台。人工智能对话可以成为你的空房间——一个让你练习直到它不再令人感到恐惧的地方。

sentences.en: But, remember, the point of learning English is to use it in the real world, and even though an AI tutor might feel comfortable, reassuring, and familiar, its only value is in helping you prepare for the real world, real conversation.
sentences.zh: 但是，请记住，学习英语的目的是在现实世界中使用它，尽管人工智能导师可能会让人感觉舒适、安心和熟悉，但它的唯一价值在于帮助你为现实世界、真正的对话做好准备。

sentences.en: And the longer you postpone that, the more scary it will be, no matter what your “pronunciation score” is on your favourite app.
sentences.zh: 你推迟这一步的时间越长，它就会越可怕，无论你在最喜欢的应用上的“发音得分”是多少。

sentences.en: And, by the way, you don’t have to use any kind of third-party app to “chat with AI”.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，你不需要使用任何第三方应用来“与人工智能聊天”。

sentences.en: Most of the big AI companies will have a “voice mode”, so just open that up and start talking.
sentences.zh: 大多数大型人工智能公司都有“语音模式”，所以只需打开它并开始说话即可。

sentences.en: You don’t need to pay for anything else unless you really want to.
sentences.zh: 除非你真的很想，否则不需要为其他任何东西付费。

sentences.en: And a quick practical tip here is to set it up properly before you go into voice mode, so type out whatever you want to practise first, and any prompt instructions, then switch to voice.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个简短的实用小贴士：在进入语音模式之前先把它设置好，先打出你想练习的内容以及任何提示指令，然后再切换到语音。

sentences.en: Now, I know we’ve talked about quite a lot here.
sentences.zh: 好了，我知道我们在这里讨论了很多内容。

sentences.en: It can sound overwhelming, so many different potential tools, chatbots, AI-tutors, vocabulary apps, apps that promise to personalise your English learning.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能让人应接不暇，有这么多不同的潜在工具、聊天机器人、人工智能导师、词汇应用、承诺个性化你英语学习的应用。

sentences.en: The truth is that there is still one thing that matters more than all of this: consistency.
sentences.zh: 事实是，仍然有一件事比所有这些都更重要：坚持。

sentences.en: Actually consuming and then producing English regularly, daily if possible.
sentences.zh: 定期消费然后产出英语，如果可能的话每天都进行。

sentences.en: Someone who listens to podcasts, BBC News, and reads an English-language newspaper every day without ever touching AI will make far faster progress than someone who spends weeks researching which AI-tutor to subscribe to, then downloads five and waits for the perfect moment to start.
sentences.zh: 一个每天听播客、BBC 新闻并阅读英语报纸从不碰人工智能的人，其进步速度会远快于那些花几周时间研究该订阅哪个 AI 导师、然后下载了五个并等待完美时机开始的人。

sentences.en: And let me end this by talking about my own personal experience here, as I am actively learning Swedish.
sentences.zh: 最后，我想结合我个人学习瑞典语的亲身经历来谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: As you might imagine, I have all sorts of AI companies contacting me and offering me things to promote their app, so I have loads of free accounts.
sentences.zh: 正如你所想象的那样，我有各种各样的人工智能公司联系我，提供各种东西让我推广他们的应用，所以我有很多免费账号。

sentences.en: And the truth is that I barely use them.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，我几乎不用它们。

sentences.en: I listen to Swedish podcasts, I try to read real Swedish, I go to Swedish class.
sentences.zh: 我听瑞典语播客，我试着阅读真实的瑞典语，我去上瑞典语课。

sentences.en: I use AI to get feedback on my writing, to explain grammar points to me, and I sometimes talk to ChatGPT in Swedish.
sentences.zh: 我使用人工智能来获取对我的写作的反馈，向我解释语法点，我有时会用瑞典语和 ChatGPT 对话。

sentences.en: Perhaps this makes me old-fashioned, but I know firsthand that actually doing the work is far more important than how you do the work.
sentences.zh: 也许这让我显得老派，但我亲身体会到，真正去做比你怎么做远为重要。

sentences.en: Learning English, like any language, is about consistency, attitude, and materials that interest you.
sentences.zh: 学英语，和学任何语言一样，关乎坚持、态度以及你感兴趣的材料。

sentences.en: AI won’t make you fluent. But it can make consistent learners even more effective.
sentences.zh: 人工智能不会让你流利。但它能让坚持学习的人更有效率。

sentences.en: OK, then, that is it for today's episode on AI & Learning English in 2026.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天的关于 2026 年人工智能与英语学习的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one and that you've learnt something new.
sentences.zh: 希望这期节目很有趣，并且让你学到了新东西。

sentences.en: As always, I would love to know what you thought of this episode.
sentences.zh: 和往常一样，我很想知道你对这期节目的看法。

sentences.en: How, if at all, do you use AI to improve your English?
sentences.zh: 你是如何（如果真的有的话）使用人工智能来提高英语的？

sentences.en: What are your tools of choice? Plain old ChatGPT, or something else?
sentences.zh: 你首选的工具是什么？老式的 ChatGPT，还是别的什么？

sentences.en: You can head right into our community forum, which is at community.leonardoenglish.com and get chatting away to other curious minds.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接进入我们的社区论坛，网址是 community.leonardoenglish.com，与其他充满好奇心的头脑畅所欲言。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你刚才收听的是由 Leonardo English 制作的《English Learning for Curious Minds》。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，注意安全，我们下期节目再见。
